key_insight: WildASR is a multilingual diagnostic benchmark sourced from real human speech that systematically isolates failure factors, revealing substantial real-world ASR degradations missed by curated benchmarks.
problem_solved: ASR evaluations that look near-human on curated tests fail to expose which languages, conditions, or factors cause degradation in deployed voice agents—practitioners lack diagnostic tools to anticipate and quantify these failures.
method: Assemble WildASR: a four-language dataset drawn entirely from real human speech covering diverse recording devices, environments, accents, and utterance types.
Annotate and organize data around diagnostic factors (noise, channel, speaker variation, language) and define an evaluation protocol and metrics to isolate their impacts.
Benchmark multiple ASR systems across factors to quantify performance gaps and provide analysis tools for targeted failure-mode diagnosis.
impact: WildASR enables engineers and researchers to pinpoint where and why ASR systems fail in realistic settings, guiding robust model development, targeted data collection, and safer deployment of voice agents.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing word-error-rate (WER) across the four languages and common noise/channel conditions to highlight performance gaps.
Heatmap (factors × models) showing error amplification by diagnostic factor (e.g., accent, device, environment) for quick failure-mode identification.
Dataset composition infographic (pie/stacked bars) showing language breakdown, device types, and environment categories to convey benchmark realism.
Flow diagram of the evaluation pipeline: data collection → annotation by factor → controlled evaluation → failure analysis, to show reproducibility and usage.
paper_title: Back to Basics: Revisiting ASR in the Age of Voice Agents
paper_authors: Geeyang Tay, Wentao Ma, Jaewon Lee, Yuzhi Tang, Daniel Lee
